name: Indium
occurrence: Rare and dispersed, recovered mainly as a by-product of zinc ore processing.
majorUses: Indium tin oxide (ITO) transparent conductive coatings on touchscreens and LCDs
notableCharacteristics: Named for the brilliant indigo line it produces in a flame spectroscope, which is how it was discovered.
whyHere: Its softness and low melting point come from a metallic bonding structure weaker than its neighbours, and it's exactly this along with its transparent-conducting oxide form that makes it essential to every touchscreen you've ever tapped.
didYouKnow: Nearly every smartphone, tablet, and flat-screen TV touchscreen relies on a thin transparent layer of indium tin oxide to sense your finger's location — indium's supply has become a genuine tech-industry concern.
genZNote: You are literally touching indium right now if you're reading this on a touchscreen. No exceptions.
